title: Turnover package and validation documents | Aquemi
meta: Every document we deliver, by stage: URS matrix, P&IDs, EN 10204 3.1 certificates, weld log, FAT and IQ/OQ. Request a redacted sample package.
eyebrow: DOCUMENTATION · EU GMP ANNEX 15 · GAMP 5 · ASME BPE · 21 CFR PART 11
headline: Every document your auditor will ask for, issued as we build and indexed to your URS
lead: At installation qualification (IQ) your team checks the system against its drawings, certificates and specifications; when a document is late, IQ waits. We write the package as we design, fabricate and test, send each document for your review at the stage that issues it, and hand over one turnover package indexed to your user requirement specification (URS): material certificates to EN 10204 3.1, weld logs to ASME BPE, and factory acceptance test (FAT) and installation and operational qualification (IQ/OQ) protocols your quality unit approves before execution (EU GMP Annex 15, 2.6). Check the format first: request a redacted sample.

secondary_cta.label: See the standards each document proves

blocks.h: The package is the record your inspector reads
body: An inspector does not test your water system. They read its record: why each design decision was made, what each part is made of, how each weld was inspected and which test proved each requirement. At IQ your team checks the installation against that record, line by line (EU GMP Annex 15, 3.9). When a document is missing or late, IQ waits for it, and so does your release.

So we write the package as we go. Each document is issued at the stage that produces it, goes to your team for review while the work is still open, and lands in one turnover package indexed to your URS. The index below is the full list: every document our system and service pages promise, what it proves, when you see it, its format and who approves it. Your proposal lists the subset that applies to your system.

blocks.h: How each document reaches your file

items.d: Issued at the stage that produces it, with a document number, revision and the URS or functional specification clauses it answers.
Your team comments within the review turnaround agreed at kick-off, [standard review period, working days] unless your procedures set another.
We answer each comment in a comment log, revise and reissue. The log stays with the document.
Protocols are approved by your quality unit before execution. Specifications and plans are approved at the design gate they belong to.
Executed records carry results as found, raw data and both parties' signatures. Drawings are reissued as built.
The register lists every document and its current revision. A document still open at handover is a punch list item with an owner and a date.

blocks.body: If your site has protocol templates, numbering and good documentation practice rules, we write the FAT, SAT, IQ and OQ protocols in them. If not, we use ours, built on EU GMP Annex 15, GAMP 5 and the ISPE commissioning and qualification guides. Either way every test case carries a URS or functional specification reference, so it lands in your traceability matrix.

blocks.h: Questions validation and quality teams ask

items.q: Can we see real documents before we order?
items.a: Yes, redacted. The sample turnover package above shows the index, protocol contents and record formats from a delivered system, with customer names and data removed. [Confirm which samples are shared openly and which under NDA.] Your QA team can also audit how the records are produced: [what an audit covers, for example the fabrication shop and document control].

items.q: When do we see the protocols?
items.a: The FAT protocol reaches your quality unit [protocol issue before FAT, weeks] before testing, for approval before execution (EU GMP Annex 15, 2.6). IQ and OQ protocols follow the FAT, so they can reference its results rather than repeat them.

items.q: Can FAT results count towards qualification?
items.a: Where your quality unit agrees, yes. EU GMP Annex 15, 3.6 lets FAT tests stand where transport and installation cannot affect them, and the ISPE approach leverages engineering tests carried out under good documentation practice. We mark candidate test cases in the C&Q plan at detailed design, so the leverage is planned, not argued afterwards. Water quality on your feed is never leveraged.

items.q: Do you check third-party certificates, or just forward them?
items.a: We check them. At receipt, material markings are checked against the certificate [PMI, standard or option], and the material log ties each product-contact component to its EN 10204 3.1 certificate by heat number. Certificates are delivered as the issuer sent them, never retyped, so your reviewer sees the original.

items.q: Are your electronic signatures 21 CFR Part 11 compliant?
items.a: [State the electronic signature method used on protocols and reports, and whether it meets 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GMP Annex 11, 14.] Part 11 applies to how your site uses the records. If your procedures require it, we execute protocols in your electronic validation system under your accounts, or sign in wet ink and scan.

items.q: Do we own the native files?
items.a: [State what the customer receives: drawing formats (PDF and native CAD), ownership or licence terms, and the design software used.] The PDF set in the turnover package is yours to keep and reproduce for your records either way.

items.q: Is the documentation available in French?
items.a: [Confirm which documents are offered in French, for example the operation and maintenance manual, SOP drafts and training material, and how translations are reviewed.] For a system installed in Quebec, your legal team can tell you which documents the Charter of the French language requires in French.

items.q: What happens to the package after handover?
items.a: It stays current. Every service visit adds a signed report, calibration certificates and a parts record; every change adds updated as-builts, an updated dead leg register and change-scoped test records. Aquemi keeps a copy for [retention period, years], so a lost document can be reissued.
